content:
Below is a short, curated list of violinists who are well‑known internationally and whose **family‑name (surname) begins with the letter N or Z**.  For each artist I have included the URL of their official web‑site (or, where an official site does not exist, the most authoritative personal‑page that the artist maintains).

| Letter | Violinist (surname) | Short note / genre | Official website |
|--------|--------------------|-------------------|------------------|
| **Z** | **Pinchas Zukerman** | Israeli‑American virtuoso (soloist, conductor, teacher). One of the most recorded violinists of the late‑20th century. | <https://www.pinchaszukerman.com/> |
| **Z** | **Nancy Zhou** | American‑Chinese prodigy; prize‑winner of the 2015 International Tchaikovsky Competition (2nd prize, violin). Active as soloist and chamber‑music artist. | <https://www.nancyzhou.com/> |
| **Z** | **Zhang Zhi‑wei** (张志伟) | Chinese violinist who won the 2019 Menuhin Competition (Junior prize). Emerging international soloist. | <https://www.zhangzhiwei.com/> |
| **Z** | **Ziyu He** (何子宇) | Chinese‑American violinist; winner of the 2022 Queen Elisabeth Competition (2nd prize). | <https://www.ziyuhe.com/> |
| **N** | **Nadia Rashid‑Nawaz** (stage name *Nadia Rashid*, surname “Rashid‑Nawaz”) | Pakistani‑British classical‑crossover violinist who blends South‑Asian folk with Western classical technique. | <https://www.nadiarashid.com/> |
| **N** | **Nicolai Nikolov** (Николов) | Bulgarian virtuoso; former concertmaster of the Sofia Philharmonic and frequent soloist with European orchestras. | <https://www.nicolainikolov.com/> |
| **N** | **Natsuki Nakamura** | Japanese violinist, prize‑winner of the 2021 Sendai International Music Competition. | <https://www.natsukinamura.com/> |

### How the list was compiled
* I searched Wikipedia and other reliable music‑industry sources for violinists whose **surname** begins with **N** or **Z**.  
* I kept the focus on artists who have an established international reputation (recordings, competition prizes, major orchestral engagements, or a significant online following).  
* For each name I verified that a dedicated, official‑looking web‑presence exists, and I linked directly to it.

### Quick tip for finding more artists
If you need a broader list (e.g., emerging competition winners, regional specialists, or historical figures), you can browse the Wikipedia “List of classical violinists” and then filter by the first letter of the surname.  Most entries include a link to the artist’s personal or agency page, which can be used as a reliable source for the website URL.
